lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to implement binary search on a sorted list using low, high and mid, and compare its efficiency with linear search.
If a list is sorted, you can be clever: check the middle.
If the target is bigger, throw away the lower half; if smaller, the upper half.
Keep low and high at the ends of the part still possible. mid = round((low + high) / 2).
Binary search finds any number in 1–100 in at most 7 steps, and in a million items in at most 20.
Linear search could take a million.
Binary search gives wrong answers on unsorted data.
That’s one reason sorting matters so much.
In Python, binary search is a while loop with low, high and mid — exactly the same idea.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
